project.name: Fast-print denture base resin
project.concept_label: Concept: project workspace for Claude Science (unofficial)
project.synthetic_label: Synthetic data · stress haystack (250 trials, eval only)

objective.label: Viscosity ≤ 1.5 Pa·s
objective.why: Thinner resin recoats faster between layers, so dentures print faster.

guardrails.label: 3-pt bend
guardrails.source_note: Modeled on ISO 20795-1 denture-base values; verify before quoting.

guardrails.label: Bubbles (porosity)
guardrails.plain: Few bubbles in the cured part

guardrails.label: Cytotoxicity
guardrails.plain: Safe for cells: at least 70% survive

stations.label: Weigh
stations.card: Weigh base monomer, diluent and photoinitiator into a 50 g batch. The balance logs each addition, so the recipe is recorded as weighed, not as planned.

stations.label: Mix
stations.card: Mix at 3000 rpm for 2 minutes, per SOP v1. The mixer logs speed, duration and when the run ended.

stations.label: Degas
stations.card: Pull a vacuum on the mixed resin so trapped bubbles expand and escape. Not in SOP v1, and the degasser has no data interface, so it's only logged if someone writes it on their worksheet.

stations.label: Viscosity
stations.card: Measure viscosity at 25 °C. This is the objective: at most 1.5 Pa·s.

stations.label: Print
stations.card: Print 6 tensile dogbones and 3 bend bars. The printer logs when each job starts, which is how the rest time between mixing and printing is known.

stations.label: Post-cure
stations.card: Post-cure under UV at 60 °C for 45 minutes. The oven has no interface, so the time is entered by hand.

stations.label: Test
stations.card: Pull and bend the printed parts, image a cross-section for bubbles, and run the cell-viability assay. Results land in the log automatically.
